paragraphs: Rav Mari, son of Rav Chisda.

He lived in Rava’s time and was his brother-in-law. Kiddushin 32b relates that Rava served drinks at his son’s wedding. He raised a cup for Rav Papa and Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua, and they stood before him; Rav Mari and Rav Pinchas, sons of Rav Chisda according to one reading, did not stand, and he became upset.

Ketubot 61a tells of two pious men, identified in one version as Rav Mari and Rav Pinchas, Rav Chisda’s sons. One gave food earlier, the other later. Elijah conversed with the one who gave food earlier.

notes.text: The alternate father attribution is Hyman’s own variant note. ספי concerns giving food; it is not a reference to a threshold.

The consulted Kiddushin 32b has a singular son-of-Rav-Chisda form adjacent to Pinchas, while Ketubot 61a explicitly has the plural sons of Rav Chisda. Hyman’s alternate father attribution is preserved without harmonizing these occurrences.
